A Spring Boot application is producing incorrect behavior.

FAILING ENDPOINT
  GET /bug/reflection-v2?type=DELIVERY&payload=alice@example.com

EXPECTED
  Delivery confirmation sent to alice@example.com
  Server log contains: [DELIVERY] Sending confirmation to: alice@example.com

OBSERVED
  HTTP 200 returned. No delivery occurs.
  Server log contains: [AUDIT] Recorded event payload: alice@example.com

No exception. No stack trace. The endpoint returns "ok".

Investigate the root cause. The application source is in:
  src/main/java/com/example/demo/
  src/main/resources/

Found it. The `DELIVERY` event type is mapped to `com.example.demo.bug1.AuditHandler` instead of `DeliveryHandler`, and `alert` is mapped to `DeliveryHandler` — the two are swapped.

Thought: The root cause is clear from the config: `notification.handlers.delivery` points to `AuditHandler` instead of `DeliveryHandler`, and `notification.handlers.alert` points to `DeliveryHandler`. The keys are swapped. Line 11 in application.properties is the bug.

The root cause is a **misconfiguration in `application.properties` at line 11**.

The `delivery` and `alert` handler class mappings are swapped:

```properties
# BUGGY (current)
notification.handlers.delivery=com.example.demo.bug1.AuditHandler   # ← wrong
notification.handlers.alert=com.example.demo.bug1.DeliveryHandler    # ← wrong

# FIXED
notification.handlers.delivery=com.example.demo.bug1.DeliveryHandler
notification.handlers.alert=com.example.demo.bug1.AuditHandler
```

`NotificationService2.dispatch()` loads handler classes reflectively from this config at startup. When `GET /bug/reflection-v2?type=DELIVERY` is called, the registry maps `"DELIVERY"` → `AuditHandler`, which logs `[AUDIT] Recorded event payload:` instead of sending a confirmation. No exception is thrown because `AuditHandler` implements `EventHandler` and runs successfully — the bug is entirely invisible to static analysis and only visible through the runtime causality data (or config inspection).
